description: Theseus kills the Minotaur using Ariadne's thread. But he forgets to change the sails: his father Aegeus throws himself into the sea, which still bears his name.

hero.hook: A monster in a maze. A thread to get out. Forgotten sails that baptize a sea.

blocks.text: **Theseus**, founding hero of Athens, confronts the **Minotaur**, a half-man, half-bull creature hidden in the  of Crete. The story combines courage, romantic cunning and family tragedy. [[Labyrinth]]
By killing the monster, Theseus frees Athens from a bloody tribute. But a forgotten detail, black sails instead of white, will cost his father his life and give his name to the Aegean Sea.

King **Minos** of Crete refuses to sacrifice a white bull to **Poseidon**, god of the seas. To take revenge, Poseidon inspires in Queen **Pasiphaé** a passion for the animal. The Minotaur is born. Minos tasks the inventor  with building a prison with no escape: the Labyrinth. [[Maze]]

blocks.caption: The Minotaur, locked in the Cretan Labyrinth.

blocks.text: Crete then dominates the sea: a . After a lost war, Athens must hand over every nine years **seven young men and seven young girls** as food to the monster. On the third delivery, **Theseus**, son of King **Aegean**, volunteers. [[Thalassocracy]]
Aegeus and Theseus agree on a signal: **white** sails if the hero returns alive, **black sails** if he is dead. This detail will decide a drama.

sections.title: The Minotaur and the tribute of Athens

blocks.text: In Crete, **Ariane**, daughter of Minos, falls in love with Theseus. She knows that strength is not enough in the Labyrinth. With the help of Daedalus, she gives him a ball of wool: . He attaches it to the entrance and unwinds the thread as he moves forward. [[Breadcrumbs]]

blocks.caption: Ariadne gives Theseus the thread that will save his life.

blocks.text: Theseus kills the Minotaur, then rewinds the thread to get out. He flees with the young Athenians and Ariadne. But on the island of **Naxos**, he leaves her sleeping. Some say the god **Dionysus** wanted her as his wife. Ariadne, desperate and then deified, receives a golden crown that has become a constellation.
The return should be a celebration. Intoxicated by victory or troubled by Ariadne's abandonment, Theseus forgets to hoist the white sails. The ship approaches Athens under black sails.

blocks.caption: Cape Sounion, from where Aegeus watched for the return of his son.

blocks.text: At **Cape Sounion**, the old king Aegeus scans the horizon. He only sees the blackness of mourning. Convinced that his son is dead, he throws himself from the cliff. The sea has since been named: the **Aegean Sea**. Theseus arrives king... and orphaned by his own negligence.
The “ship of Theseus” has become a philosophical paradox: if we replace all the planks one by one, is it still the same boat?

sections.title: The black sails of Cape Sounion

blocks.text: Crowned, Theseus becomes an organizing king.  is attributed to him: the unification of the towns of Attica around Athens. He established the , major city festivals. Might combines with right. [[Synoecism]] [[Panathenaea]]

His reign includes other adventures, such as the fight against the . But the Labyrinth remains its mark: knowing how to unravel the inextricable, while remaining vulnerable to oblivion. Theseus forges the greatness of Athens from the ashes of a family tragedy. [[Amazons]]
**Theseus** kills the **Minotaur** thanks to **Ariane**'s thread. By forgetting to change the sails, he causes the suicide of his father **Aegean**, who gives his name to the Aegean Sea.
